sourceDirectedNegativeEdges.actualIndividualCoreContrastAndBoundary: Land/locality versus company/shrine are the introductory cores. A shrine occupies land, but the setting and the institution are not identical; this is not all-senses separation.
Land/locality versus serving/performing work. Working locally does not make the action identical with the location; no universal separation of every compound is claimed.
Land/locality versus principle/logic. 地理 is a whole geography word; its two components are not interchangeable definitions of that whole.
Younger brother versus strong. A younger brother can be strong, but the relative sibling relation and the quality are different represented cores; 弓 is an indexing/shape connection.
Younger brother versus man/male. A younger brother is male, so the category relationship is real; the contrast is the specifically younger sibling relation, not universal semantic disjointness.
Younger brother versus south. This is a relative-family versus direction core contrast, not a historical explanation of similar strokes.
Strong versus younger brother, separately considered in this direction. A sibling can possess strength; that shared context does not equate the quality and relationship.
Strong versus principle/logic. A strong argument can be logical, but neither a quality of force nor coercion automatically means the argument's principle.
Strong versus turning/rolling. Strong force can cause rolling; that causal situation does not equate the two displayed cores or establish all-sense separation.
Light/clear versus reflecting/projecting an image. Brightness and reflection share a visual domain; this is only an introductory core distinction, not universal optical separation.
Light/clear versus clothing. Clothing can be light in color, but the quality is not the clothing noun; word-bound medicine/obedience meanings of 服 are not erased.
Light/clear versus use/purpose. Clarity can concern a purpose, but the represented quality and use are different; no universal sense inventory is claimed.
Reflecting/projecting an image versus English/outstanding. Shared エイ and the modern 央-like component do not make the represented cores identical; 英's flower-domain meaning remains attested.
Reflecting/projecting an image versus time/hour. A film has a duration, but the imaging action is not the time unit.
Reflecting/projecting an image versus day of the week. Shared 日-like shape and a screening schedule do not equate the displayed meanings.
Day of the week versus time/hour. These belong to the same temporal domain at different levels; not universal temporal disjointness or ordinary fallback approval.
Day of the week versus learning/practising. A weekly practice schedule and superficially similar upper strokes do not equate the represented cores.
Day of the week versus light/clear. Luminary/brightness senses remain in the official character evidence; only the displayed weekday and clarity cores are contrasted.
Clothing versus moon/month. Preserve the shared classical 月 key without inferring a moon-origin story or equating the clothing and lunar/time cores.
Clothing versus morning. Dressing in the morning is a shared situation, not lexical identity; the court/dynasty meanings of 朝 remain word-bound.
Clothing versus paper. Both can be materials, but the displayed garment and paper cores differ; this is not an exhaustive judgment about compounds.
Morning versus light/clear. Mornings can be bright and 明 has dawn/opening uses; the temporal and quality cores are related, not universally disjoint.
Morning versus clothing, independently considered in this direction. Morning dress is a shared context, not identity of the represented meanings.
Morning versus turning/rolling. The time of an action is not the action itself; no etymology is inferred from shared modern strokes.
Work/occupation versus music/pleasure/ease. Work can be enjoyable or musical and religious uses remain word-bound; this is not work-versus-fun universal separation.
Work/occupation versus tree/wood. Woodworking is an activity, not proof that a material and work have identical cores; modern shape is not the whole meaning.
Work/occupation versus collecting/gathering. Gathering can be work and collections can contain works; retain the shared activity domain, not an all-senses exclusion.
Music/pleasure/ease versus work/occupation, separately judged in this direction. Enjoyable work and specialized religious words prevent a universal opposition.
Music/pleasure/ease versus study. Study can be enjoyable and both have ガク in compounds; neither shared reading nor situation equates the represented cores.
Music/pleasure/ease versus east. Similar modern tree-like lower shapes do not equate the meanings or prove historical derivation.
Principle/logic versus field/open country. A field can be an object of reasoning, but the conceptual and landscape cores are not identical; no transitive guard follows.
Principle/logic versus heaviness/layering. A weighty argument is a contextual connection, not proof that the represented cores are the same.
Principle/logic versus land/locality, separately considered. 地理 is a whole word; its existence does not equate its component meanings.
Flower versus north. A flower can grow in the north; botanical object and direction remain different represented cores.
Flower versus old/ancient. An old flower has an age, but that quality is not its botanical identity; no all-senses claim is made.
Flower versus water. Flowers need water; the association is real but not identity of the flower and water nouns.
English/outstanding versus tea. English tea is a shared cultural/compound context, not identity of language/excellence and the drink; botanical senses remain available.

UNRESOLVED: the displayed English/outstanding title differs from flower, but actual 英 has a flower-domain meaning and はなぶさ is attested with 花房/英. A title distinction or an unsupported rarity claim CANNOT establish a safe negative pair for a bare written prompt. Actual independent disposition is required; no ordinary-safety or provisional qualified guard approval is given here.

English/outstanding versus reflecting/projecting an image, separately considered. Shared エイ and shape do not equate the represented cores; this is not a judgment that all 英 senses are language-related.
Tea versus English/outstanding, separately considered. The English-tea association is not lexical identity; 英's flower-domain meanings remain a limitation, not erased by its title.
Tea versus flower. Tea plants flower, and both are botanical, so this is a drink/tea versus flower introductory contrast, not universal botanical separation.
Tea versus music/pleasure/ease. Drinking tea may be pleasant, but the drink and that quality/activity are different represented cores.
Turning/rolling versus vehicle. Wheels/vehicles can turn and roll; the motion and the object are related, not universally disjoint.
Turning/rolling versus carrying/luck. Movement domains and 運転 overlap; this is only the represented rotation-versus-transport/fortune core contrast, not all-senses ordinary safety.
Turning/rolling versus morning, separately considered in this direction. The motion may occur in the morning, but its time does not define the motion.
Field/open country versus principle/logic. A field may be studied logically; the setting is not the conceptual principle.
Field/open country versus heaviness/layering. Shared modern lower/left shapes and a heavy object in a field do not equate the displayed cores.
Field/open country versus movement. Activity can occur in an open field; location and motion are related contextually, not identical meanings.
Collecting/gathering versus bird. The attributed bird/tree account connects the concepts, but a bird is not the gathering action; 隹172 is not 鳥196.
Collecting/gathering versus tree/wood. Birds can gather in a tree; the action and the location/material do not have identical cores.
Collecting/gathering versus work/occupation, separately considered. Gathering can be work and literary collections contain works; not universal action/work separation.
